Learning objectives quality.criterion_text: Every objective is specific, measurable, and includes enough context that an implementer could design a check script to verify it. Objectives collectively describe a coherent skill set, not isolated facts.

Appropriate for audience.criterion_text: Objectives are precisely calibrated and explicitly note which skills are new to learn versus prerequisite skills the audience already has. The difficulty gradient is intentional and visible.

Audience definition.criterion_text: Clear skill level, specific prerequisites (named skills or tools, not just "familiarity with"), and assumed knowledge documented. A content author could independently judge explanation depth.
Audience definition.finding: Fixed: removed the unused "editing a one-line config" prerequisite (no challenge involves file editing) and replaced with "backgrounding a process", which Challenge 1 actually requires.

No assumed knowledge beyond prerequisite.criterion_text: Prerequisites are comprehensive and verifiable. Every concept the track uses is either listed as a prerequisite or explicitly planned as a learning objective. The boundary is airtight.

Challenge roadmap progression.criterion_text: Deliberate progression where each challenge's goal requires skills from prior challenges. The roadmap reads as a narrative arc. A reader could predict what the next challenge covers based on the learning trajectory.

Challenge dependencies.criterion_text: Airtight prerequisite chain. Every concept is fully planned before it is referenced. Dependencies are explicit in the roadmap, not implicit.

Progressive complexity.criterion_text: Clear progression from guided to independent. The roadmap indicates that scaffolding will decrease as skills are established.
Progressive complexity.finding: Difficulty labels progress basic->basic->intermediate->intermediate; acceptable but scaffolding decrease is implicit rather than explicitly called out.

Challenge scope balance.criterion_text: Consistent challenge scope where each challenge has a clear, achievable goal completable in a focused session. Balance is driven by learning coherence, not symmetry.

Timelimit settings.criterion_text: Timelimits are precisely calibrated per challenge based on expected steps. Simple challenges get shorter limits, complex challenges get proportionally longer ones. The values reflect actual task duration estimates, not uniform defaults.

Difficulty progression labeling.criterion_text: Difficulty labels are precise, consistent with challenge content, and form a visible gradient. Labels help learners set expectations and help authors calibrate explanation depth.

Slug naming conventions.criterion_text: Slugs are concise, descriptive, and form a readable table of contents on their own. The naming pattern is uniform and the slug alone conveys the challenge's purpose.

Resource specification.criterion_text: Resources are functional but not optimized -- over-provisioned machines, unnecessary VMs, or images larger than needed for the workload.
Resource specification.finding: Fixed: added explicit --network host decision for the Management Center container (so it can reach the host-native Hazelcast member) and explicit process-backgrounding (nohup ... & for the JVM, docker run -d for Management Center) so the single terminal tab stays usable across all 4 challenges.

Image selection.criterion_text: Smallest appropriate image for each resource. Specific version tags chosen to match the track's content exactly. Image choices minimize startup time and resource consumption.

Port and service exposure.criterion_text: Every service tab has a corresponding port exposed. Port numbers match the actual service configuration. No unnecessary ports exposed.
Port and service exposure.finding: Fixed: clarified that --network host exposes port 8080 directly on the VM's network namespace, so no separate -p mapping is needed.

Cloud account configuration.criterion_text: Least-privilege IAM configuration. Permissions are precisely scoped to the track's needs with no excess access. Region selection optimizes for availability and cost. Quota limits are explicitly considered.

overall.finding: Fixed: Cleanup section and Caveats now commit to a concrete, verbatim defensive restart-if-not-running block that Challenges 2-4's setup scripts must include, resolving the previously-unfulfilled nohup-across-challenge-boundaries risk instead of merely flagging it.

review_history.note: track:review-challenge-plan flagged (1) cognitive-load bundling in steps 1 and 3, (2) unresolved nohup-across-challenge-boundaries risk (cleanup:none with no committed downstream fix). Verbatim reuse of Ch1's defensive-restart block: pass. 'Zero license prompts' claim in Step 7 was phrased as a graded confirmation with no check backing it (score 3). Iframe/CSP risk was an acceptable, well-reasoned deferral (not blocking). Fixed: reworded Step 7 to explicitly label the license-prompt observation as not auto-graded, so learner-facing text no longer overstates what Check verifies.

CLC syntax verified plausible/consistent; INSERT-vs-SINK idempotency divergence in solve script judged sound and non-corrupting. Gaps found: (1) check-workstation only verified 1 of 5 taught currency rows despite assignment's 'five currencies' completion marker -- fixed to require all 5 rows + count>=5, mirrored in solve's confirmation loop; (2) Management Center defensive block mislabeled as a 'verbatim' Ch2 contract when Ch2 never established one (it was adapted from Ch2's solve script) -- comment corrected; (3) setup's map-clear 'verification' only re-ran clear rather than confirming emptiness -- fixed to assert map size=0 for both maps; (4) assignment never warned that INSERT INTO is append-only/errors on re-run -- added an explicit note after the Step 5 command.

Unconditional re-seed via clear+idempotent-rewrite (never INSERT INTO) verified sound for all 3 possible Ch3-data-survival scenarios. Check/dashboard split correctly mirrors Ch2's disclosed-limitation pattern. Track-completion-via-Check-passing-plus-closing-paragraph judged reasonable given the track's declared no-editor-infrastructure scope. SINK INTO/clc map remove judged properly scaffolded as new vs. Ch3's confident-reference commands. Final cross-challenge holistic pass (Ch1-4) found no inconsistencies in defensive-restart contracts, tab reuse, terminology, or timing. One gap: check-workstation never verified the untouched greeting 'en' entry survived removal/addition of 'fr'/'es' -- fixed by adding a dedicated Check 4 (renumbering Checks 4-6 to 5-7, TOTAL_CHECKS 6->7) and mirroring the same assertion in solve's confirmation loop.

live_playthrough_fix_2026_07_15.symptom: CREATE OR REPLACE MAPPING / INSERT INTO both failed with 'ERROR The Jet engine is disabled.'
live_playthrough_fix_2026_07_15.root_cause: Hazelcast's SQL engine runs on top of the Jet execution engine, which is OFF by default in the embedded jar's bundled hazelcast-default.yaml (confirmed by extracting the real 5.7.0 jar: 'jet: enabled: false'). Adding hazelcast-sql-5.7.0.jar to the classpath (the earlier fix) was necessary but not sufficient -- Jet itself still had to be turned on. The Docker image's own bundled config (hazelcast-docker-assembly.yaml) has 'jet: enabled: true' baked in, which is why this only surfaces for the embedded/plain-JAR path this track deliberately uses in Challenge 1.
live_playthrough_fix_2026_07_15.fix: Added '-Dhz.jet.enabled=true' as a JVM system property to every place the member is started: 01-run-hazelcast-community-edition/{assignment.md Step 3, setup-workstation, solve-workstation, check-workstation fail-message}, and the duplicated defensive-restart blocks in 02/03/04's setup-workstation. Per Hazelcast's own error-message documentation, this system property is honored specifically because HazelcastMemberStarter loads config via Config.load().
